title: Exact coarse correlated equilibrium is approximate
statement: Let $G$ be a finite two-player game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column actions, and let $\sigma$ be a joint distribution over the action profiles $(i,j)$ that is a coarse correlated equilibrium of $G$; that is, neither player can increase their expected utility under $\sigma$ by committing in advance to a fixed pure action, so that for every row action $i'$ the row player's utility from deviating to $i'$ (against the column marginal of $\sigma$) is at most their expected utility under $\sigma$, and likewise the column player's utility from deviating to any fixed action $j'$ (against the row marginal of $\sigma$) is at most their expected utility under $\sigma$. Then for every real $\varepsilon \ge 0$, the distribution $\sigma$ is an $\varepsilon$-coarse correlated equilibrium of $G$: each player's gain from any such unilateral pure deviation exceeds zero by at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: σ is a coarse correlated equilibrium of G
replaced:
If $\sigma$ is an exact CCE of $G$ and $\varepsilon \ge 0$, then $\sigma$ is
also an $\varepsilon$-CCE of $G$.
